subject: Discovery recap — observability playback & eval plan
message_1_headers:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sasha Kim <sasha.kim@atlasai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery recap — observability playback & eval plan
message_1_body:
Hi Sasha,

Thanks again for taking the time today — it was really helpful to see how Atlas AI is using multiple open models for search expansion and contextual generation. Below is a concise recap so our teams are aligned and we can move toward a focused PoC.

Top pain points you called out:
- Sporadic quality regressions when you switch model families (high variance in hallucination rate).
- No end-to-end tracing from request -> generated tokens -> user action; hard to tie model decisions to product metrics.
- Lack of real-time dashboards for production evals and latency SLO tracking (you rely on ad-hoc notebooks).
- Cost concerns when peak traffic trips larger model variants; want graceful fallbacks.

Success criteria you mentioned:
- Visibility: dashboards showing per-route latency (p50/p95), error rate, and rerank/quality delta by model variant.
- Traceability: distributed tracing hooks that include prompt hash + input metadata and KV-cache correlation.
- Evals: a golden prompt set (~50–100 seeds) and nightly regression alerts when eval metrics drop >3%.
- Ops: automated fallback to cheaper model variant when p95 latency >150ms and no drop in quality >2%.

Immediate next steps (we agreed):
1) I will share a short proposal with a sample playback dashboard and a recommended eval seed set (attached).
2) Rishi/Neha to propose a lightweight tracing hook implementation and a list of headers/metadata Atlas needs to capture.
3) Schedule architecture deep-dive with your infra team (tentative: Dec 15) to scope the PoC and connectivity needs (VPC peering / private deployment constraints).
4) We will provide a preliminary sizing & cost estimate for a 4-week PoC including a simple canary rollout guardrail.

Attachments included: redwood-playback-dashboard-proposal.pdf (PDF), atlas-eval-seed-prompts.csv (CSV) — both are draft templates you can edit.

If I missed anything or you want different success criteria captured, call it out and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll send the PoC proposal by EOD Tuesday.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

---

message_2_body:
Thanks Logan — this is great and captures everything. A few clarifications from our side:

- Golden prompt set: we can provide 60 seeds across three product areas (search expand, FAQ, and summary). We want to preserve user privacy so will scrub PII; will drop the CSV into the Drive link you shared.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 150ms is correct for the core search flow; summary flow can tolerate up to 300ms.
- Tracing hooks: we need the prompt hash + model variant + request_id in our logs to correlate to user sessions.

Next steps for us: I’ll drop the seed prompts by COB Mon and invite infra leads (Evan, Priya) to the Dec 15 deep-dive. If you can include a quick mock of the regression alert threshold I can pass that to our SRE.

Sasha Kim
Head of Product | Atlas AI

message_3_body:
Looping you both in with a few prep items before the Dec 15 architecture session. Please keep this internal.

Quick notes:
- Tracing hooks: propose capturing these fields per request: request_id, prompt_hash, model_name, model_config (quantization flag), kv_cache_hit (bool), upstream_route. That should let us replay playback traces tied to eval hits.
- Dashboard tiles to include in the PoC: per-route p50/p95 latency, token-cost per response, quality delta by model (A/B compare), nightly eval pass rate, active fallbacks count.
- Golden set handling: recommend we accept Atlas seed CSV, add our canonical metadata columns (seed_id, intent_tag, domain) and store in a read-only folder for nightly eval runs.
- Rollout guardrails: canary 10% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback if nightly eval score drops >3% OR if p95 latency increases >20% vs baseline.

I attached a one-page mock for the playback dashboard to reference (will replace with final).

Neha
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
